meta.notes: This manifest is the system-of-record the Video Factory reads from. Each character's canonical_reference must be locked to ONE approved image before it is used to generate episode scenes, so the character stays visually identical across the whole series.

lock_log.why: Selected to match SWRS live client mix - healthcare and dental, property management, and trades/construction were together more than half of the last 60 signings.
lock_log.note: Patty, Rachel and Cody needed a restyle pass; their off-model first attempts are recorded under superseded so they are never picked up by mistake.

lock_log.why: Steven asked for two new episodes built around the paperwork obstacles; the Invoice Monster had no reference image, so it could not be used until locked.
lock_log.note: Two designs were produced and both approved: A as primary (compact creature), B as the fully grown form.

lock_log.why: Steven cast a separate voice for what had been filed as the Invoice Monster's grown form, which makes it a distinct character. Promoted to its own entry with its own locked reference and name.
lock_log.note: First two speaking characters in the series: Invoice Monster (Vlad) and Filing Cabinet Phil (Vera).

continuity_rules: These characters are assets. Always maintain their core appearance, personality, and voice.
Do not change hair, eye color, body type, or signature clothing.
Always use SWRS brand colors where shown (cool blue palette: navy #070B97, blue #0446F1, sky blue #0495F1).
Keep logo placement consistent on clothing and props.
Lock ONE canonical reference image per character; generate every future frame against it.
Characters never lip-sync in narrated episodes; they emote and gesture while an external narrator speaks.

episode_engine.formula: Obstacle (the problem) -> Persona (who feels it) -> Hero/AI Guide (the easy fix) -> Success Character (the payoff/CTA)
episode_engine.personas_are: audience segments / who the episode is aimed at
episode_engine.heroes_are: recurring leads and guides who deliver the resolution
episode_engine.success_characters_are: the closing payoff beat and CTA
episode_engine.core_cta: Getting your accounts to SWRS is easier than you think. Send your first accounts today.

example_episodes.fix: place by email, skip the portal

characters.name: Invoice Monster
characters.title: Represents Aging Receivables
characters.one_liner: Grows as invoices age. Shrinks when accounts are placed. One of him is almost endearing.

canonical_reference.design: a shaggy hunched creature built entirely from layered invoice sheets and manila statements, cream and manila paper tones with navy printed ruling lines, bold red PAST DUE and OVERDUE rubber stamps used as markings, two big round googly cartoon eyes peering out from a fringe of paper, wide goofy grin, stubby arms of stapled sheets. No fire, no scales, no wings, no tail - deliberately distinct from the Late Fee Dragon. Where the dragon SITS ON the paperwork, the Monster is MADE OF it.
canonical_reference.world: Reference framing matches the Late Fee Dragon: in-scene hero shot in a dim open-plan office at night lit by cool blue monitor glow, stylized non-photorealistic Pixar-style 3D.

primary.note: Variant A - client-selected. Compact creature form; the default for episode work because it has a body, arms and a face that can emote across scenes.

canonical_reference.canon_rule: Grows as invoices age. Shrinks when accounts are placed.
canonical_reference.split_note: The design previously filed here as variant B was promoted to its own character, Filing Cabinet Phil, on 2026-08-09 once Steven cast it a separate voice. This entry is the small creature only.

characters.name: Filing Cabinet Phil
characters.title: Represents the Backlog
characters.one_liner: One overdue invoice is nothing. A thousand of them is Phil.
characters.personality: Patient, smug, in no hurry whatsoever. Time is on his side and he knows it.
characters.catchphrase: Take your time. I've been growing.
characters.relationship: Formed when Invoice Monsters pile up. Collapses back into them when accounts are placed.

canonical_reference.design: a tall precarious tower of overdue statements and manila folders with a bent-staple paperclip crown, cream and manila paper tones, navy printed ruling lines, red PAST DUE and OVERDUE rubber stamps as facial markings, two big round cartoon eyes near the top of the stack and a wide goofy grin, sheets fanning out at the sides as stubby arms. No fire, no scales, no wings, no tail.
canonical_reference.world: Reference framing matches the Late Fee Dragon and the Invoice Monster: in-scene hero shot in a dim open-plan office at night lit by cool blue monitor glow, stylized non-photorealistic Pixar-style 3D.
canonical_reference.design_note: NAME/DESIGN MISMATCH, accepted by Steven: the name says filing cabinet, the locked design is a paper stack. Kept deliberately - Phil is what staff call the pile, not a literal cabinet. If a future episode needs an actual cabinet, this reference must be re-locked, not quietly reinterpreted.

(job d67dddeb) and EP-022 'I just wanted to be one invoice again.' (job d3174a66); both episodes rebuilt on fresh IDs same day.

brand_audio.chosen_by: Steven (picked candidate D from six auditioned vibes: playful-pizzicato, corporate-piano, marimba-fintech, cinematic, retro-funk, acoustic-folk)
brand_audio.style: light cinematic animated-film score: sprightly staccato strings, playful woodwinds, soft glockenspiel, gentle closing brass swell; ~108 bpm, instrumental, no vocals

extended.use: long episodes EP-004/008/012 (same prompt, separate rendition)

brand_audio.mix_rule: bed at 0.18x under the -14 LUFS master mix, 0.4s fade-in at 0s, 0.8s fade-out ENDING BEFORE each episode's brand card so the logo reveal stays silent (23s episodes: fade st=18.9; EP-004 st=22.6; EP-008 st=22.7; EP-012 st=24.4), amix normalize=0 + alimiter 0.95.
brand_audio.ownership: original generated composition, SWRS-owned; no third-party license required
